Let \(p=503\). We only need the values of \(S_r\) modulo \(503\).

Consider the polynomial

\[
(1+x)^{10000}=\sum_{k=0}^{10000}\binom{10000}{k}x^k
\]

and reduce it modulo \(x^{502}-1\) over the field \(\mathbb F_{503}\).  
When we reduce powers of \(x\) modulo \(x^{502}-1\), the coefficient of \(x^r\) becomes exactly

\[
\sum_{\substack{0\le k\le 10000\\ k\equiv r\pmod{502}}}\binom{10000}{k}
\pmod{503},
\]

which is \(S_r \pmod{503}\).

Now work in characteristic \(503\). By the freshman’s dream,

\[
(1+x)^{503}=1+x^{503}.
\]

But since \(x^{502}\equiv 1\pmod{x^{502}-1}\), we have

\[
x^{503}=x\cdot x^{502}\equiv x.
\]

Therefore

\[
(1+x)^{503}\equiv 1+x \pmod{x^{502}-1}.
\]

Now

\[
10000=19\cdot 503+443.
\]

Thus

\[
(1+x)^{10000}
\equiv \bigl((1+x)^{503}\bigr)^{19}(1+x)^{443}
\equiv (1+x)^{19}(1+x)^{443}
= (1+x)^{462}
\pmod{x^{502}-1}.
\]

Since \(462<502\), the polynomial \((1+x)^{462}\) has no exponents that wrap around modulo \(502\). Hence its coefficient of \(x^r\) is

\[
\binom{462}{r}\quad\text{for }0\le r\le 462,
\]

and is \(0\) for \(463\le r\le 501\).

So

\[
S_r\equiv
\begin{cases}
\binom{462}{r}\pmod{503}, & 0\le r\le 462,\\[4pt]
0\pmod{503}, & 463\le r\le 501.
\end{cases}
\]

Because \(503\) is prime and \(503>462\), none of the binomial coefficients \(\binom{462}{r}\) is divisible by \(503\). Therefore the only multiples of \(503\) occur for

\[
r=463,464,\dots,501.
\]

There are

\[
501-463+1=39
\]

such integers.

\[
\boxed{39}
\]
